reviewer: Codex root, independent second AI-assisted source/target comparison

findings.fix: Romans8:13 is a conditional statement, not the same imperative form as Colossians3:5.
findings.before: Both command putting to death what belongs to disordered bodily conduct. Romans says the body's practices by Spirit; Colossians names earthly members and immediately lists vices. The objects and means are not rewritten as one phrase or a command literally to destroy the believer's body.
findings.after: Both speak of putting to death disordered bodily conduct. Romans states conditional life/death alternatives and names acting by Spirit; Colossians directly commands putting to death earthly members and lists vices. The objects and grammatical forms remain distinct, without making either text a direction literally to destroy the person's body.
findings.resolution: Applied an explicit conditional-versus-imperative distinction after complete actual source/target reading.

findings.fix: Keep the actual supplied beyond words formulation rather than narrowing it to wordless.
findings.before: This chapter describes intercession by both the Spirit and Christ Jesus. Here the Spirit helps weakness and intercedes with wordless groanings; the later verse names the dead-and-raised Christ at God's right hand. The related intercession roles do not identify the Spirit as the crucified person or give Christ this verse's groanings.
findings.after: This chapter describes intercession by both the Spirit and Christ Jesus. Here the Spirit helps weakness and intercedes with groanings beyond words; the later verse names the dead-and-raised Christ at God's right hand. The related intercession roles do not identify the Spirit as the crucified person or give Christ this verse's groanings.
findings.resolution: Applied the saved source wording in the explanation; source and target bodies are unchanged.

review_notes: Every complete source unit and actual retained target/context passage was read. Hosea2:25 says mercy/Not Shown Mercy where Romans9:25 says beloved/not beloved; Hosea2:1 retains its actual Greek-based identity. Genesis25:23 says greater/lesser where Romans9:12 says older/younger.

Exodus9:16 says you were preserved where Romans9:17 says I raised you up. Isaiah8:14 retains its conditional not-stumbling statement, while Romans9:33 positively names a stumbling stone; Isaiah28:16 says trusts in it rather than believes in Him. None of these actual differences is silently harmonized.

Romans9:22 has an unspecified fitting agent for wrath-vessels;9:23 explicitly names prior preparation of mercy-vessels. The comparison keeps different grammatical roles and does not fill the former from the latter. John10:29 retains What My Father has given Me as its actual subject.
